verdictAmendedByM26-5.supersedes: The `verdict` and `productionChangesAllowed` fields above described the state at b136f44 and are retained verbatim, not overwritten. A reader must take THIS object as current.
verdictAmendedByM26-5.why: INV-M5 verbatim: 'production_changes_allowed stays false until F1–F8 all pass.' F8 was the sole FAIL; M26-5 closed it, and all eight now PASS. Leaving the flag false would be an editorial override of a written invariant, exactly as leaving it true prematurely would have been.
verdictAmendedByM26-5.whyANewLabel: Neither label the integration doc names fits. `PENDING_FINAL` is DEFINED there as 'F1–F8 unmet' (§5.4, line 53) and is now false by its own definition. `IMPLEMENTED_NOT_PUBLICLY_CLAIMED` presupposes an implementation that does not exist — no M batch has changed a single line of runtime. This label is therefore NOT one of the two upstream-named states; it is introduced here because the honest state falls between them, and it is flagged as an addition rather than passed off as existing vocabulary.

whatItUnblocksAndWhatItDoesNot.unblocked: The FINALITY precondition on M26-1…M26-4. They may now be authorized on their merits.
whatItUnblocksAndWhatItDoesNot.notAuthorized: Nothing is authorized BY this flag. M26-1 additionally requires its own ADR (0063 — 0062 was consumed by the T0 landing decision) and an explicit batch authorization. A gate ceasing to block is not a decision to proceed.
whatItUnblocksAndWhatItDoesNot.stillForbidden: Every item on new17 §19's forbidden-copy list. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` remains 2024-11-05, and no public surface may claim 2026-07-28 support — that claim needs an implementation, not an evidence lock. Asserted by a gate, not just stated: tests/invariants/mcp-spec-vendor.invariants.test.ts pins the served constant, in the very file that could otherwise read as permission.

verdictAmendedByM26-5.unevenEvidenceQuality: All eight PASS, but not on equal footing, and averaging them would hide that. F1, F2, F3, F4, F7 now rest on digest-locked bytes a gate re-reads every CI run. F5 (transport/auth/cache semantics) and F6 (the tasks extension) still rest on the 2026-08-08 manual read of pages NOT vendored here — their evidence is normative prose across many spec pages, and vendoring the whole documentation tree was out of scope for M26-5. So the gap NARROWS from 'nothing is re-checkable' to 'two of eight are not'. Recorded rather than smoothed over; closing it means vendoring those pages, which is a scoping decision for a later batch.

verdictBasis.summary: F8 is the only FAIL. F1-F7 were measured PASS against primary upstream sources on 2026-08-08.
verdictBasis.whyStillPending: INV-M4 requires finality be evaluated over VENDORED bytes, never a live fetch. No vendored copy exists (third_party/ measured ABSENT), so no gate in this repo can re-evaluate F1-F7 offline. The upstream revision is ready; our evidence base is not.
verdictBasis.narrowedFrom: docs/new16-new17-execution-status.md:103-113 listed all eight gates as unverified and derived PENDING_FINAL from that. Seven of those eight are now measured PASS. The verdict is unchanged but its REASON narrows from 'upstream may not be ready' to 'we have not vendored the bytes' — which is a step only this repo can take.
verdictBasis.unblockingAction: M26-5 (vendor the spec bytes under third_party/ with a digest lock). This confirms O-M1's default of 'lock first' on measured grounds rather than editorial preference.

vocabularyMapping.hazard: The word 'Final' means OPPOSITE things in new17's F1 and in the upstream versioning vocabulary. Reading upstream's 'not Final' as an F1 failure imports someone else's vocabulary into our criterion.
vocabularyMapping.upstreamFinalMeans: past, complete specifications that will not be changed (i.e. frozen and superseded)
vocabularyMapping.f1FinalMeans: published and citable rather than draft/RC
vocabularyMapping.measured: 2026-07-28 is upstream 'Current'. Under upstream's vocabulary it is deliberately NOT 'Final'; under F1's criterion it PASSES.
vocabularyMapping.consequence: A future reader of this file must not invert F1 by applying the upstream glossary to it.

gates.requirement: The revision is published (not draft/RC) and citable

evidence.observation: The versioning page defines three revision states (Draft / Current / Final) and names 2026-07-28 as the CURRENT protocol version.
evidence.caveat: See vocabularyMapping — upstream 'Final' denotes a frozen past revision, so 'Current' is the strongest state a live revision can hold.

gates.requirement: The version string is stable and citable

evidence.observation: Version string is the date form 2026-07-28 (YYYY-MM-DD). Upstream states the version will NOT be incremented for changes that maintain backwards compatibility, so the string is a stable anchor.

gates.requirement: A schema artifact is retrievable and summarizable

evidence.observation: The specification page names specification/schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts as the authoritative schema for the revision.
Two enumerable sections exist: Key Changes and Deprecated Features.

amendedByM26-5.verdict: PASS stands — a changelog snapshot IS retrievable, which is all F4 requires.
amendedByM26-5.correction: The observation above is FALSE as written. Neither 'Key Changes' nor 'Deprecated Features' appears in the bytes, and there are seven sections, not two.

amendedByM26-5.originalRetained: The original observation is preserved above verbatim rather than overwritten, per the append-amend discipline ADR 0061 §8.5 established: a record of what we believed is evidence about our method, and deleting it would hide the very drift this batch demonstrates.

gates.requirement: Transport / auth / cache semantics are normative

evidence.observation: Per-request version declaration via the io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion _meta key; MCP-Protocol-Version header on Streamable HTTP; UnsupportedProtocolVersionError for mismatch. All expressed in MUST-level BCP-14 wording.

gates.qualifier: normative but NOT part of core

evidence.observation: Tasks are specified as an EXTENSION: opt-in, negotiated during initialization. The semantics are normative within the extension; a core-only implementation is conformant without them.
evidence.consequence: Any future CallLint claim about task semantics must be scoped to the extension, never stated as core protocol support.

evidence.observation: The deprecation registry lists 6 deprecated features and an EMPTY Removed section. The earliest possible removal is the first revision on or after 2027-07-28, so nothing breaks within this revision.

amendedByM26-5.verdict: PASS stands. The substance of the observation is confirmed; its attribution and one sub-claim are corrected.

sourceMisattributed.detail: The changelog has NO 'Removed' heading at all and 4 numbered deprecation items. The registry is a separate page: `## Deprecated` with exactly 6 feature rows, plus `## Removed` reading 'No features have been removed under this policy yet.' The count and the empty section were right; the URL pointed at a page that cannot support either. This is why deprecated.mdx is vendored — an evidence artifact whose source URL is wrong is not re-checkable.

subClaimOverPrecise.asRecorded: The earliest possible removal is the first revision on or after 2027-07-28.
subClaimOverPrecise.asMeasured: True of 4 of the 6 rows. `includeContext: "thisServer"/"allServers"` reads 'Follows Sampling (SEP-2577)', and HTTP+SSE transport reads 'Three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final' — a date the registry does not record and that this repository cannot compute.
subClaimOverPrecise.whyTheVerdictSurvives: F7 asks whether a breaking ERRATUM is pending, and deprecation is not removal. Upstream states a Deprecated feature 'remains part of the specification but is scheduled for removal', that earliest removal only marks ELIGIBILITY, and that the actual removal is a Core Maintainer decision taken during release preparation — i.e. an act of a FUTURE revision. The Removed section is empty. So nothing breaks within 2026-07-28 on either clock, and the unrecorded SEP-2596 date cannot move the verdict; it bounds only how precisely the sentence may be phrased.
subClaimOverPrecise.forwardObligation: Any future CallLint copy about 2026-07-28 deprecations must not state a single uniform removal date. Two of the six clocks are relative, and one of those two depends on an upstream event with no published date.

evidence.observation: third_party/ measured ABSENT on b136f44 (`ls -d third_party` → no such directory).
evidence.consequence: INV-M4 forbids CI fetching the live spec, so with no vendored bytes there is no offline basis for F1-F7. Their PASS above rests on a one-time manual read recorded here, NOT on a repeatable gate.

closedByM26-5.inv-M4: Honoured. The fetch happened once at authoring time and is pinned to an immutable commit; the gate reads only committed bytes. The prohibition is on CI fetching, which is what makes vendoring the remedy rather than the violation.
closedByM26-5.whatChangedForF1-F7: Their VERDICTS are unchanged — vendoring re-confirmed all seven. What changed is their standing: F1, F2, F3, F4 and F7 now rest on committed bytes a gate re-reads on every CI run, where before they rested on a dated manual read. F5 and F6 still do NOT: their evidence is normative prose on pages not vendored here (transport/auth semantics; the tasks extension). Recorded as a narrowed gap rather than presented as fully closed.
closedByM26-5.whatItCaughtImmediately: Two of the seven recorded observations were falsified by the bytes on first read — F4's section names, and F7's source URL plus its uniform-date sub-claim. Both had survived a merged batch. This is the measured argument for O-M1's 'lock first' default: the errors were not in the verdicts but in the evidence, and only committed bytes could expose them.
